subject: Question on how prompt-state / prefix cache hits are billed + request for baseline rate card

Subject: Question on prompt-state/prefix cache billing and baseline rate card

Hi Vanessa / Aditya,

Quick intro — I’m Oliver (Head of ML Ops at EdgeAI). We’re evaluating Redwood for a pilot to replace our current hosted serving layer. One key question that came up from our infra and finance teams: how do you handle billing when a request hits a prompt-state / prefix cache? Specifically:

- If a user sends a repeated prefix (same initial context) and Redwood serves the response from a cached KV/state, do you still bill input tokens for that prefix?
- Is there a different treatment if the hit happens within the same session/connection vs across separate API calls from different clients?
- Any per-request baseline/overhead charges we should anticipate even if the heavy inference is avoided by cache?

We’re sizing for ~3B tokens/month initially with burstable spikes. Before we loop in procurement, could you send a baseline rate card and a short note clarifying the cache-hit billing semantics? Also interested in any discount thresholds for committed volume.

Hi Oliver —

Thanks for the clear questions. I’m attaching our baseline rate card (PDF) and a short summary below to get us started. Aditya (cc) can add the technical details about caching semantics.

High level summary:
- Baseline billing: we bill per-token for both inputs and outputs by default.
- Prefix/prompt-state cache: when a request can be satisfied from a server-side prefix (KV) cache without re-executing full attention computation, compute cost is reduced; for commercial customers we offer two common billing options — standard (token-based) and cache-optimized (agreed upon carve-outs on repeated prefixes).
- Per-request overhead: there's a small fixed request charge (listed on page 2 of the rate card) to account for RPC, logging, and storage access regardless of compute used.

Suggested next step: 30-minute sync where Aditya can walk through specific cache scenarios for your workload and we can scope a pilot and discount tier. Are you available Thursday afternoon PT?

Hi Oliver — quick tech note to supplement Vanessa’s summary. I’ll keep it pragmatic.

What we run that matters for billing:
- Client request arrives with full prompt. We compute a hash for the prefix/state and check our distributed prefix KV cache. If there’s a valid cache hit that contains model KV state for the matching model variant + sequence length bucket, we can avoid re-running the attention/transformer decoder for those prefix tokens.

Billing behavior (default offering):
- Input tokens: billed for each request by default. This keeps accounting simple and predictable across customers and aligns with downstream observability.
- Output tokens: billed as usual.
- Cache hit discount mechanics (commercial/negotiated): we offer an optional cache-hit credit that effectively reduces the billed input-token footprint for repeated prefixes. In the cache-optimized plan we can discount or zero-rate repetitive prefix tokens when the server-side KV entry is reused within the agreed policy window.
- Request overhead: a small fixed per-request fee applies in both cases.

Policy nuances:
- Session vs cross-session: the cache is keyed by prefix hash + model variant + customer id. So hits can occur across separate API calls and across different clients as long as the key matches and the cache entry is valid. Session affinity is not required for a hit.
- TTL and eviction: entries have TTLs tuned for production workloads; we can configure longer TTLs for dedicated/private deployments as part of a contract.
- Compliance customers: for customers that require complete determinism / logging of every token we may disable cache-hit suppression — in those cases billing reverts to token-based for all requests.

Commercial suggestions for EdgeAI (given your ~3B token estimate):
- Pilot: allow up to 100k prefix hits/week with cache-hit credits (no input-token billing on those prefixes) so you can validate economic impact.
- Commit tier: for a 12-month $Xk/mo commit (we can put numbers in a MAP), we’d include a cache-hit carve-out that excludes up to Y% of repeated prefixes from input-token billing.

I don’t want to bake numbers here without Vanessa but happy to join a call and walk through a couple of real queries from your traffic.

1) If two different model variants are functionally compatible (e.g., same architecture and tokenization) but live under different model ids in the catalog, does Redwood share cache entries across those ids, or would that be a miss?
2) For the pilot you suggest, can you include example contractual language that states 'cache-hit prefix tokens will not be billed for the duration of the pilot' so our procurement team has something to review?
3) Can you provide a sample invoice or audit showing how a prior customer’s prefix-hit credits were applied (redacted of course)? Procurement wants evidence.

If you can send the pilot SOW + sample invoice we’ll loop in procurement (procurement@edgeai.com) and legal.

Hi Oliver / procurement team —

Thanks — answers inline and next steps below.

1) Cross-model sharing: we do not automatically share prefix entries across distinct catalog model ids. Cache entries are scoped to model id + quantization variant + sequence bucket. If you need cross-variant sharing we can discuss a one-off mapping or a shared-cache policy for the MAP.

2) Pilot SOW: attached is a short MAP/SOW template that includes the pilot language you requested: 'During the pilot period (30 days), prefix-cache hits defined by matching prefix hash will be excluded from billed input tokens up to 100k hits/week.' We can edit the time window or hit cap per your needs.

3) Sample invoice: happy to provide a redacted invoice showing applied cache-hit credits — we’ll pull a recent example and share it under NDA / redaction.

Next steps:
- I’ve attached EdgeAI-MAP-v1.docx (short form) with a proposed pilot clause.
